title: Dataverse goes where you build: Copilot Cowork, coding agents and n8n
summary: Dataverse for Copilot Cowork, coding agents and n8n: one set of skills and guardrails across Cowork, GitHub Copilot, Claude, Codex, Cursor and more.
body_markdown:
Developers rarely pick one tool and stay in it. A single week might include coding agents in the IDE, a terminal agent for quick tasks, an automation platform for integrations, and an AI assistant for everything in between. However, business data should not get harder to reach as that list grows. That is why we keep bringing[Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-intro) to the coding agents and platforms where you already build.


In July, we[expanded the Dataverse plugin for coding agents](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/blog/2026/07/06/dataverse-july2026/) to Claude, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, and we committed to supporting more. Since then, Dataverse has arrived in[Copilot Cowork](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/cowork/) , in more coding agents and in[n8n](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.microsoftdataverse/) . This post brings the full picture together in one place.


## Where Dataverse runs today: Copilot Cowork, coding agents and n8n


Here is where Dataverse is available today, and how to add it on each platform. Each listing installs the same open-source[Dataverse skills](https://github.com/microsoft/Dataverse-skills) .


Platform How Dataverse shows up How to get it


[Copilot Cowork](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/cowork/cowork-plugins) Dataverse plugin Open Customize, select Microsoft Dataverse, then select Connect


GitHub Copilot Dataverse plugin` /plugin install dataverse@awesome-copilot`


Claude Code Dataverse plugin` /plugin install dataverse@claude-plugins-official`


OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT Dataverse plugin Search for Microsoft Dataverse in the OpenAI plugin directory, or run` codex plugin add dataverse@openai-curated`


Cursor Dataverse plugin` /add-plugin dataverse` , or go to Settings, then Plugins, and search the Marketplace for Dataverse


Gemini CLI Dataverse extension` gemini extensions install https://github.com/microsoft/Dataverse-skills --skip-settings` , then set your environment URL with` gemini extensions config dataverse DATAVERSE_URL --scope workspace`


Google Antigravity Dataverse plugin` agy plugin install https://github.com/microsoft/Dataverse-skills/tree/main/.github/plugins/dataverse`


[n8n](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.microsoftdataverse/) Built-in Microsoft Dataverse node Add the Microsoft Dataverse node to any workflow


For any other agent that reads local skills, one command installs every Dataverse skill:` npx skills add microsoft/Dataverse-skills -s "*"` . Full instructions for each platform are in the[Dataverse skills repository on GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/Dataverse-skills) .


## Copilot Cowork: governed apps from a single prompt


The Dataverse plugin in[Copilot Cowork](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/cowork/) brings Dataverse skills to a conversational, approval-driven experience. You describe an app in plain language. Then Cowork designs the tables and relationships, reuses existing tables such as Contact, and seeds sample data. Finally, it builds and publishes a working app in[Microsoft Copilot Managed Runtime (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/managed-apps/?view=o365-worldwide) . Every change comes to you first as an approval card, and every action runs with your own permissions.


For a full walkthrough and demo, read the companion post,[From one prompt to a governed Dataverse app: the Dataverse plugin lands in Copilot Cowork](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/blog/?p=135388) .


## n8n: a native Dataverse node for your workflows


[n8n](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.microsoftdataverse/) is where many developers connect apps, APIs and AI agents into workflows. Dataverse is now a[built-in node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.microsoftdataverse/) there, so there is no custom HTTP plumbing to write.


In the video, the n8n AI Assistant builds a multi-channel lead-capture workflow in seconds. Leads arrive from a web form, WhatsApp, Telegram or Facebook. Next, an AI step extracts the details. Then one Dataverse node checks for an existing lead, and a second Dataverse node creates the lead if it is not there yet. This is the pattern we see most often: read trusted context from[Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-intro) , act on it, and write the result back. All of it happens inside the automation platform the team already uses.


Beyond the demo, the Microsoft Dataverse node can create, update, upsert, get, get many and delete rows in standard and custom tables through the[Dataverse Web API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/overview) . For example, Get Many supports column selection, OData filters, sorting, expand and[FetchXML](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/fetchxml/overview) . Table and column pickers also load straight from your environment’s metadata. Meanwhile, the Microsoft Dataverse OAuth2 credential supports both delegated user access and app-only access. Every operation and option is documented on the[Microsoft Dataverse node page in the n8n docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.microsoftdataverse/) .


## The same Dataverse skills across coding agents


Under the hood, every coding agent integration is built from the same[open-source skills](https://github.com/microsoft/Dataverse-skills) . As a result, the experience stays consistent wherever you work. A connect skill handles one-time setup and authentication. Specialist skills then cover the rest of the job:


- Querying records and bulk data import
- Data modelling for tables, columns, relationships, forms and views
- Solution lifecycle
- Security roles and access
- Environment administration
- Finance and Operations X++ development and deployment


In addition, an overview skill routes each request to the right specialist. Behind the scenes, the plugin picks the right tool for each job. That might be the[Dataverse MCP server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp) , the[Dataverse CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/dataverse?activeTab=readme) , the[Python SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/sdk-python/overview) or[PAC CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/cli/introduction) .


Most importantly, the guardrails travel with the skills. The plugin follows a[least-privilege model](https://github.com/microsoft/Dataverse-skills/blob/main/docs/safety-and-guardrails.md) , so it cannot exceed the permissions of the signed-in user. Dataverse authorizes every API call on the server. Credentials stay in the operating system’s secure credential store or in memory. Finally, the only telemetry is application-level metadata. It excludes prompts, tool arguments or record data.


## Why Dataverse belongs wherever you build


[Dataverse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-intro) already holds the records, relationships and rules that run the business. It is also built into Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot Studio and Dynamics 365. Agents and automations are only as good as the context they work with. So our job is to make that same context available wherever developers and makers build, with enterprise security intact. Each added surface is one less reason to copy data somewhere else. In turn, it is one more place where the same trusted data model does the work.


We are not done yet. Tell us which platform you would like to see next. You can also contribute skills or improvements directly[on GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/Dataverse-skills) .
